title: Midwest Art History Society publishes Volume 3 of Venue, a peer-reviewed online open access journal
summary: Announcing the publication of the third volume of Venue , the peer-reviewed and edited online journal of the Midwest Art History Society. It is free and available to the public sponsored by the Texas Digital Library - Open Journal Systems. The journal fulfills its promise in providing scholars and researchers in the arts access to new discoveries and new perspectives on works of art and has additionally highlighted exhibitions and curatorial accomplishments across the United States. While maintaining the highest standards of quality, the journal is also committed to providing opportunities for new voices and perspectives. Rather than adopting a thematic approach, this volume highlights the work of both junior and senior scholars, reflecting the mentoring mission of MAHS in supporting the next generation of art historians and curators. Emerging Scholars Distinguished Presentation Award

title: A remarkable new book explores the life, art, and enduring legacy of an Indian modernist
summary: Some artists create images that stay with us long after we have looked away. Tyeb Mehta was one of them. His paintings, with their fractured bodies, falling figures, powerful bulls, and startling fields of color, have an emotional intensity that is difficult to forget. They speak of suffering and resilience, violence and vulnerability, but also of the extraordinary human capacity to endure. A major new publication, Tyeb Mehta: Bearing Weight (with the lightness of being), offers readers an opportunity to discover the artist behind these unforgettable images and to understand the experiences, ideas, and artistic decisions that shaped his remarkable career. Published by the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art (KNMA) in collaboration with Mapin Publishing, the 240-page volume features approximately 180 illustrations and brings together important essays, archival materials, and reproductions spanning nearly six decades of artistic achievement. title: Brooklyn Museum takes a new look at Hopi Kachina dolls
summary: One of the more important Native American art exhibitions of 2026 opened at the Brooklyn Museum on October 2. Hopi Kachina Dolls: Blessings for a Balanced World brings together more than 120 works to reconsider one of the best-known—and frequently misunderstood—forms of Southwestern Native American art. At the center of the exhibition are 53 Hopi kachina dolls, or tithu, drawn from the Brooklyn Museum's extensive Indigenous collection. They are joined by historic and contemporary baskets, pottery, jewelry, photographs and other works associated with Hopi women and the Katsina tradition. (Brooklyn Museum) What makes the exhibition unusual is not simply the quality or number of objects. The curators have deliberately shifted the point of view. title: Belvedere 21 presents sixth Civa edition 'postacceleration' with five artists
summary: The sixth edition of Civa, titled postacceleration, explores a present moment shaped by the simultaneity of technological acceleration, ecological crises, political conflicts, and global flows of information. The works on view at Belvedere 21—by Eyez Li (Mingtong Li), Nolan Oswald Dennis, Kyriaki Goni, Silke Grabinger, and Letta Shtohryn—challenge the imperative of constant optimization and open up new ways of thinking about time, resonance, and resilience. News and images from around the globe reach us almost simultaneously, piling up and competing for our attention. Different temporal dynamics intersect, influence one another, and sometimes come into conflict. Rather than describing what comes after acceleration, postacceleration characterizes a present in which acceleration itself has become the norm. title: Newly available paintings by Frank Frazetta lead Heritage's November Comic Art Auction
summary: A trove of newly available Edgar Rice Burroughs-related material from renowned Burroughs collector, archivist and historian Robert “Bob” Barrett includes two paintings by his friend Frank Frazetta, which are sure to spark brutish bidding at Heritage Auctions’ Comic Art Signature® Auction, taking place Nov. 20 and 22. It’s almost a rite of passage for a young comic book or pulps fan to have a copy of his or her favorite title confiscated by a teacher disturbed by the content or annoyed by the classroom distraction. Barrett traced his fascination with Edgar Rice Burroughs’ Tarzan to a childhood chapter when a teacher snatched away his father’s copy of Tarzan and the Lost Empire, declaring no student of hers would be seen reading such a book. title: Marc Straus pairs early prints by Pop pioneers Lichtenstein and Johns
summary: The gallery is presenting Roy Lichtenstein and Jasper Johns: Early Prints, an exhibition of prints made between 1963 and 1975 by two artists who proved that the most familiar images in America were still worth a second look. Johns, whose flags and targets first appeared in 1958, tends to be described as the artist who made Pop possible. Lichtenstein, who began painting comic strip panels in 1961, is remembered as one of the artists who made it famous. The labels are useful, but they hide how much the two had in common. Both turned away from the private, gestural painting that dominated New York in the 1950s and toward images nobody had to invent: a flag, a number, a beer can, a girl crying in a romance comic. Both understood that a picture of something everyone has already seen forces a question a new image never has to answer: what has the artist added? The two artists came at printmaking

title: Daniel Rich debuts vibrant architectural cityscapes in 'Magic Mountain' at Miles McEnery Gallery
summary: Daniel Rich presents a new body of paintings in his exhibition Magic Mountain, examining themes of political power, memory, and history through nocturnal scenes of New York City. Towering buildings in rich colors of sapphire blue, amethyst purple, and tangerine fill Rich’s cityscapes with anticipation, silence, and a subtle tension suggested by an unseen activity or emptiness within. Drawing on literary themes, he considers New York as a place of reinvention while also exploring the city’s sense of isolation from the world beyond it. This is the first series Rich has made from his own photography, a nod to the artist’s authentic experience of the city he views as “something closer to a portal than to a place.” Rich refers to these cityscapes as “edited” versions of the real world. title: Ayyam Gallery marks 20th anniversary with landmark Middle Eastern group exhibition
summary: Ayyam’s 20th-anniversary exhibition seeks to honor a journey defined by continuity, resilience, and artistic exchange. Much like the gallery’s programming, the exhibition is conceived as a visceral experience, a story that has withstood the test of time. Alongside co-curators Safwan Dahoul and Ali Kaaf, director Maya Samawi aims to bring together works by all the artists who have shaped Ayyam over the past twenty years. Each curator represents a continuous artistic timeline in which the past and present complete one another and remain undeniably connected. The exhibition is accompanied by an archive that traces this history as fully as possible, not merely the story of a gallery, but of the artists, people, places, relationships, and circumstances that have shaped it. Ultimately, Ayyam’s twenty years are not merely a measure of time. They constitute a living history—one that continues to unfold. title: Ferrari at 80: RM Sotheby's returns to Maranello in 2027, marking 20 years of landmark Ferrari sales
summary: RM Sotheby’s and Ferrari S.p.A. announced a return to Maranello in 2027, marking 21 years since RM Sotheby’s first auction at the home of Ferrari. Taking place in June 2027, the sale will once again bring an exceptional selection of Prancing Horse cars in a spectacular auction to celebrate Ferrari’s 80th anniversary. RM Sotheby’s has enjoyed a close relationship with Ferrari spanning more than two decades, and during that time has been privileged to offer some of the most significant Ferraris. Since 2005, the sales held at Maranello have provided some of the most memorable moments in live collector car auction history, culminating in the spectacular 70th anniversary sale in 2017. title: Prado Museum appoints Carlos González Navarro head of 19th-century painting collection
summary: The Museo Nacional del Prado has appointed art historian Carlos González Navarro as the new head of its 19th-century painting collection, marking a new chapter for one of the museum's most important departments. He succeeds Javier Barón, who recently retired after a distinguished career at the institution. The appointment took effect on November 1, 2026, following a proposal by Prado director Miguel Falomir and approval by the Permanent Commission of the museum's Royal Board of Trustees. González Navarro will oversee the collection under the museum's Deputy Directorate for Conservation and Research. For González Navarro, the new position represents a natural progression in a career closely connected to the Prado. title: Art Institute of Chicago opens prints and drawings retrospective of Beatriz González
summary: The Art Institute of Chicago opened Beatriz González: In Series and Full Color, on view November 15, 2026 through March 1, 2027. Including more than 80 works, the exhibition will be the first prints and drawings retrospective of Colombian artist Beatriz González, whose practice spanned more than six decades until her passing earlier this year. González worked across a variety of media, but turned to drawing as the most immediate way to reflect on her experiences and to respond to events unfolding around her. Through drawings, prints, sketches, sketchbooks, objects, and archival materials, the exhibition explores her use of appropriation and repetition as formal and conceptual strategies to critically reflect on the circulation of mass-media images, notions of taste, and Colombia’s recent history. “This exhibition showcases how drawing was at the center of Beatriz’s practice, and her continuous

title: MOCA Los Angeles presents Julian Charrèire's first solo museum exhibition
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art presents Julian Charrière: Deep End, the French-Swiss artist’s first solo museum show in Los Angeles. One of two inaugural Eric and Wendy Schmidt Environment and Art Prize exhibitions presented at MOCA Grand Avenue this fall, Julian Charrière: Deep End is on view from November 15, 2026, through June 6, 2027 alongside Cecilia Vicuña’s Quipu of Encounters: The Dream of Water. Together, they reflect the Prize’s commitment to artists working at the intersections of art, climate, and environmental justice. From early works in photography and sculpture to films and newly commissioned immersive installations, Deep End demonstrates Charrière’s more than a decade-long engagement with the aesthetic and political dimensions of the natural world, considering how geological time, human history and reparative futures interrelate. title: RM Sotheby's offers 13 classic cars from The Groendyke Collection in Arizona
summary: RM Sotheby’s will offer 13 automobiles from The Groendyke Collection at its Arizona auction in January 2027, led by a 1935 Mercedes-Benz 500/540 K Cabriolet A. Bringing together rare coachwork, notable provenance, and concours-winning restorations, the offering celebrates the remarkable collecting legacy of the late John D. title: Five artists explore AI alignment and interpretability at Centre Pompidou Hanwha
summary: Hanwha x Anthropic Art Commission 2026 explores contemporary questions surrounding artificial intelligence through artistic perspectives and practices. Taking two key areas of AI research—interpretability, which seeks to understand how AI systems work, and alignment, which seeks to ensure that AI systems behave in accordance with human intentions and values—as its points of departure, the project invites artists to reconsider these questions through their own artistic methodologies. Five participating artists and collectives—MinOhrichar, Inhwa Yeom, Ubac Studio, Kahee Jeong, and Mirim Chu—present newly commissioned works that extend and reconfigure their ongoing artistic practices. title: Hauser & Wirth Somerset presents major solo exhibition by Emma Kunz
summary: This November, Hauser & Wirth presents a major solo exhibition by Emma Kunz (1892–1963), conceived in partnership with the Emma Kunz Foundation. The exhibition brings together a rare selection of works that unfold across multiple galleries, offering an insight into the visionary practice of an artist, researcher, poet and healer. Although Kunz did not identify as an artist during her lifetime, she is now recognized as a pioneering figure whose interdisciplinary work anticipated many contemporary concerns around spirituality, ecology and holistic systems of knowledge. Despite beginning her large-scale geometric drawings relatively late in life, after years of working as a healer and naturopath in Switzerland, Kunz’s interest in drawing can be traced to her early school years. title: Haines Gallery presents Deborah Butterfield's second solo exhibition of bronze horses
summary: Haines presents our second solo exhibition with Deborah Butterfield, one of the most distinctive and acclaimed sculptors of our time. Deborah Butterfield: New Work brings together a remarkable new body of bronze equine sculptures, from the monumental to intimately scaled, celebrating an artist whose singular vision has transformed our understanding of how sculpture can depict the natural world. For more than fifty years, Butterfield has dedicated her artistic practice to the exploration of material and a seemingly inexhaustible subject: the horse. Her sculptures begin as intricate assemblages of driftwood, branches, and twigs that are cast in bronze through a painstaking process that preserves the texture and character of the original materials. title: Sprüth Magers New York presents artist Thea Djordjadze's first gallery solo
summary: Thea Djordjadze’s practice is defined by sculptural environments that are continually reinvented in response to each space they inhabit. Unlikely material combinations generate tension throughout, while her ongoing investigation into institutional modes of presentation raises questions about how context shapes the interpretation and perception of art. Sprüth Magers is pleased to present A well of night, Djordjadze’s first solo exhibition at the gallery’s New York location, where new and revisited works are set into dialogue with the specifics of the neo-Renaissance-style building. Djordjadze has described her titles as sculptural in their own right, shaped to set a mood. title: Heritage Auctions offers key Golden Age Superman and Batman comic book
summary: High-grade and highly coveted copies spanning from the earliest Golden Age titles to the hottest current titles are among the most noteworthy lots at Heritage’s Nov. 19 and 21 Comic Books Signature® Auction, led by key early issues of Superman, Batman, Spider-Man and Ghost Rider titles. Fittingly, the original and ultimate comics superhero kicks off the Platinum Comics session of the Comic Books Signature® Auction opening Nov. 19 with a CGC 8.5 copy of Action Comics No. 19, the 1939 issue that was the first to be followed by a consecutive Superman cover as the Man of Steel’s popularity flew up, up and away. “Only three finer copies of this very early Superman cover exist,” says Heritage Auctions Vice President Barry Sandoval. “This is a really gorgeous copy with colors that pop off the page for stellar eye appeal.” Other high-grade

title: Paul Thiebaud Gallery presents Andrea Way's first gallery solo exhibition
summary: Paul Thiebaud Gallery announced the opening of Rhapsodies in Blue: New Works by Andrea Way. In the exhibition’s fourteen new mixed media drawings on paper, Way creates expansive abstract images through layering systemic patterning. Solely employing a symphony of blues in each work, Way’s intricate arrangements of overlays accumulate to form compositions that perfectly balance structure and beauty. The exhibition will be on view through January 9, 2027. Since 1980, Andrea Way has utilized a system called Rule-Based Drawing to create her multifaceted drawings using a diverse array of media. title: Wallace Collection examines Renaissance power in Cosimo I de' Medici display
summary: For many people, mere mention of the name ‘Medici’ automatically evokes associations with wealth, intrigue, and power – and rightly so. From the end of the 14th century, the Medici rose from provincial bankers to de facto rulers of Florence and surrounding Tuscany, with popes, grand dukes and even royalty among the scions of this remarkable family. In its latest, focused display - Cosimo I de’ Medici: Art and Dynasty - the Wallace Collection puts the spotlight on one family member who contributed significantly to their rise to fame. Through a group of five magnificent objects, including paintings, arms and armour and maiolica (earthenware), the exhibition explores how Cosimo I de’ Medici (1519–1574), Duke of Florence, first Grand Duke of Tuscany and one of the 16th century’s most powerful Italian princes, fashioned himself to legitimise

title: Green Art Gallery Dubai presents Rossella Biscotti's first gallery solo exhibition
summary: Green Art Gallery presents Centrifugal Time, Rossella Biscotti's first solo exhibition in the Gallery. The show brings together two new installations produced for the gallery, Centrifugal Gravity and The Man Who Walks Backwards (2026); early video portrait Cesar (2001); and Lucy (2026), a neon work commissioned for the 16th Gwangju Biennale. It follows her participation in Sharjah Biennial 16 in 2025, where the installation Saturated Salty Mud Stories traced the movement of materials and resources across the Gulf. At the centre of the exhibition lies Centrifugal Gravity, an installation of spherical sculptures in textile and concrete, previously produced at the Kunst-Station Sankt Peter in Cologne in 2018. title: Artist Malik Thomas Jalil Kydd debuts intimate new paintings at CARBON 12
summary: CARBON 12 presents As I Bask in Your Light, it Seeps to My Soul, Malik Thomas Jalil Kydd’s highly anticipated second solo exhibition. Bringing together works developed since the acclaimed Garden of Murmurs (2025), the exhibition marks a significant evolution in the artist's practice, one in which desire and divinity are intertwined and rendered in quiet persistence. Where previous works often situated their subjects within expansive, rolling landscapes, imbued with a mythological presence and rendered at what the artist described as "angel scale", the figures in this exhibition shift throughout domestic interiors, intimate encounters, and moments of quiet observation. title: Chilean artist Cecilia Vicuña explores Atacama water crisis at MOCA
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art presents Cecilia Vicuña’s The Dream of Water: Quipu of Encounters Maricunga. One of two inaugural Eric and Wendy Schmidt Environment and Art Prize exhibitions presented at MOCA Grand Avenue this fall, The Dream of Water is on view from November 15, 2026, through June 6, 2027 alongside Julian Charrière: Deep End, the French-Swiss artist’s first solo museum show in Los Angeles. Together, these two exhibitions reflect the Prize’s commitment to artists working at the intersections of art, climate, and environmental justice. The word quipu (kee-poo) comes from the Quechua word for “knot.” Usually consisting of colored, spun and plied thread, historic documents indicate that quipus were used for record keeping and sending messages by runners throughout the empire.
